title: Coast Guard medevacs 91-year-old man off coast of San Diego
description: Lt. Catherine Durand discusses a recent case during which a Coast Guard Sector San Diego MH-60 Jayhawk helicopter crew, along with a San Diego Fire-Rescue Department Special Tactics and Rescue (STAR) Team paramedic, medevaced a 91-year-old man from the fishing vessel Royal Star 25 miles south of San Diego Sept. 19, 2019. The man was in stable condition when he was transported to Scripps Memorial Hospital La Jolla. (Coast Guard video by Petty Officer 1st Class Patrick Kelley)
keywords: Coast Guard, medevac, rescue, San Diego
unit_name: U.S. Coast Guard PADET San Diego

transcript.text: (helicopter blades whirling)
- We got a call that someone had had a stroke,
and he needed to be medevaced to a hospital.
We were able to get there in about 15 minutes,
found the boat really easily, the rescue swimmer
was lowered down to the boat and then we lowered our litter,
which is what the patient was then hoisted
to our helicopter in, we also had a paramedic
from the San Diego Fire Department, STAR paramedic
was with us he was able to keep him stable.
Having a paramedic there, allows us to give them
higher level of care sooner, and continuously
the entire time that we are en route to drop
that patient off at the hospital.
(lively music)
So, some of the things the flight mech
has to pay attention to is how the vessel is set up,
what hazards there might be down there anything
that the hoist can get snagged on,
and the rescue swimmer has to pay attention
to how the patient is doing, as well as keeping him
the most stable as he possibly can on the way up and down.
(lively music)
It was really awesome to see the whole team
come together like that, everyone has their assigned job
and when everyone can do their job as best as they can,
it was awesome to see the entire team come together
and get that patient to the hospital quickly.
(lively music)
